documents.title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.content:
25. Usage, billing and limits

 

## What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe

 

Every feature is available on every account. Pricing is usage-based: a free monthly allowance, then metered rates for anything past it, drawn from a prepaid balance. Top-ups start at $5 and balances do not expire. Paid work stops when funds are unavailable unless optional auto-recharge adds funds.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Rates
documents.content:
### Rates

 

1,000,000 included events / month free 10 shared AI units / month included 90 day raw event retention

 

There are two units of account, events and AI units. Events are counted on one event meter: a player event or text report is 1 event, a screenshot report adds 20,000 and an MCP call is 100,000. One studio shares the monthly allowance across every project and every environment in it. Browsing saved dashboard data uses neither.

 

| What | Price | Included allowance? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Events on the meter past the allowance | $0.05 per started block of 100,000 | 1,000,000 a month |
| An AI unit past the allowance | $0.20 | 10 a month |
| Analyst question, Design chat turn, risk check, investigation analysis, digest, brainstorm question, market research run, market draft | 1 AI unit each | Yes |
| Feedback enrichment | 1 AI unit per batch of up to 25 items | Yes |
| Pattern synthesis, the deep tier | 5 AI units ($1.00) | No, prepaid balance only |
| Player Report | 1 event for the text, plus 20,000 events for a screenshot | Yes, as events |
| MCP call, read or write | 100,000 events ($0.05 past the allowance) | Yes, as events; needs an account that has funded a balance at least once |
| Source scan, first scan | $5 under 250 KB, $10 under 1 MB, $25 under 4 MB, $50 under 16 MB | No, prepaid balance only |
| Source scan, rescan | $2 while the changed source is under 250 KB, otherwise its size tier; free when nothing changed | No, prepaid balance only |
| Playtest | $1.00 a persona run, $4.00 a game profile, $5.00 a fix attempt | No, prepaid balance only |

 

Each MCP call, read or write, is metered as 100,000 weighted events on the account-wide event meter, the same meter every game's player events draw from. At 100,000 events a call, the included 1,000,000 events cover about ten MCP calls in a month when nothing else is sent, and once MCP calls have used the allowance, every game's player events are billed from the first one. The usage page in **Settings > Billing** shows MCP calls as their own bar and line, and the sidebar meter gives them their own row, with the weighted events they were metered as and what that comes to at the event rate, beside the player events and text reports your games actually sent.

 

An agent can read the same thing without the dashboard: every metered MCP answer carries `_meta.remaining`, and `get_usage_rate` returns `allowance` and `balanceCents` (see [MCP](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/#mcp)). In a rate, `includedAllowance` refers to AI units only: MCP calls draw the included monthly events first, then the prepaid balance.

 

Source scans are quoted before they run. Playtest units are charged when a job registers and refunded for any unit that did not produce a usable result, and a fix attempt is refunded in full when it changed nothing or the finding was design intent. Failed, undelivered AI work is refunded.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Rate limits
documents.content:
### Rate limits

 

Per game, per 60 second window: 60 session creations and 600 tracked events. A batch call costs one unit per event, capped at the 50-event batch ceiling, so a full batch never charges more than a valid batch could. Both the versioned and legacy ingestion paths share the same budget for a given game.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Payload ceilings
documents.content:
### Payload ceilings

 

Request bodies are capped at 100KB. Within them, an event name is capped at 200 characters and one event's data at 8KB serialized: events are gameplay facts, not documents. A batch containing one oversized event answers 400, and every SDK halves the batch until it isolates and drops the offending event automatically, so a single bloated event never costs the rest of its batch. Feedback messages are capped at 2,000 characters.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Data retention
documents.content:
### Data retention

 

Raw events are kept for 90 days. Before they age out, Ravensight extracts daily and monthly aggregates (active players, new players, sessions, events, top events, level funnels, cohort retention) and keeps those forever, along with lifetime totals per game. The 1y and All views in the dashboard, and the analyst's long-range answers, are served from these aggregates. Raw SQL via run_sql only reaches the live 90 days. History collection can be switched off per environment in **Settings > Projects**; production environments keep it on by default, development and staging environments start with it off.

 

One consequence worth knowing: the aggregates are computed from real player sessions only, and carry no column saying which rows an AI persona produced. So the long-range history endpoints take no persona scope at all, because there is nothing there to include. Your 1y and All numbers are real players, always. The **Real players** select applies to the live 90-day window.

 

Raw event export

 

```
GET /api/v1/games/<gameId>/analytics/events/export?after=0&skip=0&limit=10000
Cookie: gt_session (dashboard sign-in)

{ "events": [ { "deviceId", "sessionId", "event", "ts", "level",
               "platform", "gameVersion", "data" }, ... ],
  "nextAfter": 1755648000123, "nextSkip": 3 }
```

 

Oldest first, up to 10,000 events per page; keep requesting with `after = nextAfter` and `skip = nextSkip` until `nextAfter` is null. Events share whole-second timestamps, and `skip` is how many events at that timestamp you already have, so no page boundary drops or repeats one. Export anything you want to keep beyond the 90-day raw window.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Safety ceiling
documents.content:
### Safety ceiling

 

There is a safety ceiling of 500,000,000 events a month per account, which applies even with a balance loaded. It exists so a runaway loop or a broken build cannot turn a prepaid balance into hundreds of millions of events you never meant to send, and it is checked before anything is charged, so a refused batch costs nothing. Past it you get the same `429 quota_exceeded`, with a message saying it is the ceiling rather than the allowance. If that volume is genuinely yours, ask and we will raise it.

 

AI actions use Ravensight-managed providers and the shared prepaid balance. Customers do not supply provider API keys.
